extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent Office examiners; patent owners and practitioners involved in ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form paragraphs for conducting, corresponding in, and deciding ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings before the USPTO, including timing, amendments, service, interference, SNQ determinations, and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time in reexamination (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for extension of time in reexamination proceedings must specify the requested period of extension and must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for extension in a third party requested ex parte reexamination must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due; mere filing will not effect an extension. Requests are granted only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. See 37 CFR 1.550(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party requested ex parte extension timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension in a third party requested ex parte reexamination must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due, and the mere filing of a request will not effect any extension of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension will be granted only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. Petition fee required (37 CFR 1.17(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-owner requested ex parte extension — up to two months
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension in a patent owner requested ex parte reexamination for up to two months from the time period set in the Office action must be filed no later than two months from the expiration of the time period set in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed timely as described, may extend shortened statutory period for up to two months (subject to sufficient cause rules elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-owner requested ex parte extension — more than two months
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension in a patent owner requested ex parte reexamination for more than two months from the time period set in the Office action must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due, and the mere filing of a request for an extension for more than two months will not effect the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time for taking action in a patent owner requested ex parte reexamination will not be extended for more than two months from the time period set in the Office action in the absence of sufficient cause or for more than a reasonable time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely first response treated as request to extend shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a timely first response to this final rejection will be construed as including a request to extend the shortened statutory period for an additional two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In no event will the statutory period for response expire later than SIX MONTHS from the mailing date of the final action. See MPEP § 2265. Form paragraph may be used only in reexamination proceedings; final Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 305 — Claim enlarges scope (ex parte reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305 as enlarging the scope of the claim(s) of the patent being reexamined. In 35 U.S.C. 305, it is stated that '[n]o proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim of the patent will be permitted in a reexamination proceeding....'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim 'enlarges the scope' where the claim is broader than any claim of the patent. A claim is broader if it contains within its scope any conceivable product or process which would not have infringed the original patent; broadened if broader in any one respect even though narrower in others. Examiner should identify limitations considered to broaden scope and explain (see MPEP § 2258).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments proposed must follow 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and 1.52
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the specification and/or claims in this reexamination proceeding must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), must be formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b), and must contain any fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph may be used in order granting reexamination and/or first Office action to advise patent owner of proper manner of making amendments in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper amendment in ex parte reexamination — informality and cure
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed [1] proposes amendments to [2] that do not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), which sets forth the manner of making amendments in reexamination proceedings. A supplemental paper correctly proposing amendments in the present ex parte reexamination proceeding is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shortened statutory period for response is set; if patent owner fails to correct the informality timely, the amendment will be held not an appropriate response, prosecution will be terminated, and a reexamination certificate will issue (37 CFR 1.550(d)). Examiner notes: use for any 1.530(d)-(j) informality prior to final rejection; after final rejection, amendment should not be entered and inform patent owner using Form PTOL 467. Timeframes differ: bracket 3: one month (or 30 days) for third-party requested reexamination; two months for patent-owner requested, 35 U.S.C. 257, or Director-ordered reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission not fully responsive to non-final Office action (ex parte)
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication filed on [1] is not fully responsive to the prior Office action. The response appears to be bona fide, but through an apparent oversight or inadvertence, consideration of some matter or compliance with some requirement has been omitted. Patent owner is required to deal with the omission to thereby provide a full response to the prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shortened statutory period for response is set; failure to timely deal with omission and provide a full response will result in termination of prosecution (37 CFR 1.550(d)). Examiner should explain omitted point in bracket 2 and indicate what is needed to deal with it. Use only for responses prior to final rejection; after final rejection use advisory Office action and Form PTOL 467. Practice does not apply where omission was deliberate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of service — requirement and consequences (ex parte reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission filed on [1] is defective because it appears that the submission was not served on the [2]. After filing of a request for reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party (or parties where multiple third-party requester proceedings are merged) as provided in 37 CFR 1.248. See 37 CFR 1.550(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service and a certificate of service must be provided to the Office within ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever is longer) from the mailing date of this letter. If service is not timely made, the submission may be denied consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation (ex parte/inter partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following is an examiner’s statement of reasons for patentability and/or confirmation of the claims found patentable in this reexamination proceeding: [1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph may be used as an attachment to the Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate, PTOL-469 (or PTOL-2068 for inter partes). Any comments considered necessary by patent owner regarding the statement should be submitted promptly and labeled 'Comments on Statement of Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation' to be placed in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims held invalid by court are no longer being reexamined
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims [1] of the [2] patent are not being reexamined in view of the final decision of [3]. Claim(s) [1] was/were held invalid/unenforceable by the [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claims held invalid, patentee, decision citation, and name of court in brackets as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence and inquiry — filing channels and timeliness (EFS-Web guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence relating to this ex parte reexamination proceeding should be directed via EFS-Web, mail, fax, or by hand to specified addresses and units. For EFS-Web transmissions, 37 CFR 1.8(a)(1)(i)(C) and (ii) states correspondence (except a request for reexamination and corrected/replacement request) will be considered timely filed if (a) transmitted via Office electronic filing system per 37 CFR 1.6(a)(4), and (b) includes a certificate of transmission for each piece stating the date of transmission prior to expiration of set period in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include certificate of transmission showing date; any comments by patent owner regarding the examiner's reasons should be labeled and promptly submitted to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference request premature if examination not completed
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for interference filed [1] is acknowledged. However, examination of this application has not been completed as required by 37 CFR 41.102(a). Consideration of a potential interference is premature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2303. Use form paragraph 23.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption of ex parte prosecution after termination of interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Interference No. [1] has been terminated by a decision [2] to applicant. Ex parte prosecution is resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert interference number and whether decision was favorable or unfavorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requiring applicant to add claim to provoke interference — claim must be copied exactly; timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The following allowable claim from [1] is required to be added for the purpose of an interference: [2]. The claim must be copied exactly. Applicant is given TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of this communication to add the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal to add required claim will operate as a concession of priority for the subject matter but will not result in abandonment. Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If the interference would be with a patent, applicant must also comply with 37 CFR 41.202(a)(2) to (a)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant suggesting an interference — required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has suggested an interference pursuant to 37 CFR 41.202(a) in a communication filed [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant failed to comply with one or more of paragraphs (a)(1) to (a)(6) of 37 CFR 41.202, use this paragraph followed by one or more of form paragraphs 23.06.01 to 23.06.03 and end with 23.06.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to identify the other application or patent (interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant failed to provide sufficient information to identify the application or patent with which the applicant seeks an interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.202(a)(1) and MPEP § 2304.02(a). Use form paragraph 23.06.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to identify counts and corresponding claims (interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant failed to (1) identify all claims the applicant believes interfere, and/or (2) propose one or more counts, and/or (3) show how the claims correspond to one or more counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.202(a)(2) and MPEP § 2304.02(b). Use form paragraph 23.06.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to provide claim chart comparing at least one claim (interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant failed to provide a claim chart comparing at least one claim of each party corresponding to the count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.202(a)(3) and MPEP § 2304.02(c). Use form paragraph 23.06.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to explain in detail why applicant will prevail on priority (interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant failed to provide a detailed explanation as to why applicant will prevail on priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.202(a)(4), (a)(6), (d) and MPEP § 2304.02(c). Use form paragraph 23.06.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim added/amended but failure to provide claim chart showing written description (interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] has been added or amended in a communication filed on [2] to provoke an interference. Applicant failed to provide a claim chart showing the written description for each claim in the applicant’s specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.202(a)(5) and MPEP § 2304.02(d). Use form paragraph 23.06.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for replies in interference matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is given TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of this communication to correct the deficiency(ies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of this time period may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). (Form paragraph 23.06.06)

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not copied within one year of patent issue or publication date — pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 135(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 135(b)(1) as not being made prior to one year from the date on which U.S. Patent No. [2] was granted. Similarly, claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 135(b)(2) as not being made prior to one year from the date on which [2] was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re McGrew, 120 F.3d 1236 (Fed. Cir. 1997). For publication-based rejections use publication number and apply only if examined application was filed after publication date of the published application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority not substantiated — certified English translation required
rubrics_metrics.description: Should applicant desire to obtain the benefit of foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) prior to declaration of an interference, a certified English translation of the foreign application must be submitted in reply to this action, 37 CFR 41.154(b) and 41.202(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide a certified translation may result in no benefit being accorded for the non-English application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes reexamination — reasonable likelihood established
rubrics_metrics.description: The present request for inter partes reexamination establishes a reasonable likelihood that requester will prevail with respect to claim [1] of United States Patent Number [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.01. Note: extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted in inter partes proceedings for patent owner because 1.136 applies only to 'an applicant'; inter partes proceedings conducted with special dispatch per 35 U.S.C. 314(c); patent owner extensions under 37 CFR 1.956; extensions not available for third party requester comments because comment period is statutory 30 days (35 U.S.C. 314(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes reexamination — no reasonable likelihood established
rubrics_metrics.description: For the reasons set forth below, the present request for inter partes reexamination fails to establish a reasonable likelihood that requester will prevail with respect to at least one of the challenged claims of United States Patent Number [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue not within scope of inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An issue has been raised in the present reexamination proceeding that is not within the scope of inter partes reexamination proceedings. [1]. This issue will not be considered in the present proceeding. 37 CFR 1.906(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should identify the issues. This paragraph may be used when patent owner or third party requester raises issues such as public use, on sale, conduct, or abandonment — such issues should not be raised independently by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 314(a) — Claim enlarges scope (inter partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 314(a) as enlarging the scope of the claims of the patent being reexamined. 35 U.S.C. 314(a) states that 'no proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of the claims of the patent shall be permitted' in an inter partes reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim is broadened if broader in any one respect even though narrower in others. Examiner should identify and explain limitations considered to broaden scope (see MPEP § 2658).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period for omissions in inter partes — timing and extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period for response is set to expire (a) ONE MONTH, or THIRTY DAYS (whichever is longer), from the mailing date of this letter, or (b) after the due date for response to the last Office action, whichever is longer. THE PERIOD FOR RESPONSE SET IN THIS LETTER MAY BE EXTENDED UNDER 37 CFR 1.956.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner fails to timely supply the omission or correction and thereby provide a full response, consequences set forth in 37 CFR 1.957(b) or (c) will result. See MPEP § 2666.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Office action after inter partes order may be provided later
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office action on the merits does not accompany this order for inter partes reexamination. An Office action on the merits will be provided in due course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers to be submitted in response to action to ensure full consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure full consideration of any amendments, affidavits or declarations, or other documents as evidence of patentability, such documents must be submitted in response to this Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions after the next Office action (an Action Closing Prosecution, ACP) will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116(b) and (d), and will be strictly enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper amendment in inter partes — informality and cure
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed [1] proposes amendments to [2] that do not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j). A supplemental paper correctly proposing amendments in the present inter partes reexamination proceeding is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shortened statutory period for response is set (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer). If the patent owner fails to timely correct this informality, the amendment will be held not to be an appropriate response, and consequences per 37 CFR 1.957(b) or (c) will result (see MPEP § 2666.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) — patent owner and third party rights and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: This is an ACTION CLOSING PROSECUTION (ACP); pursuant to 37 CFR 1.951(a), the patent owner may once file written comments limited to the issues raised and/or present a proposed amendment which will be subject to 37 CFR 1.116 criteria. Such comments/amendments must be filed within 30 days or one month (whichever is longer) from mailing date. Where patent owner files such comments and/or amendment, the third party requester may once file comments under 37 CFR 1.951(b) responding within 30 days from date of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner does not timely file comments/amendment, third party requester is precluded from filing comments. Appeal cannot be taken from this action since it is not a final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) — final decision and appeal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a RIGHT OF APPEAL NOTICE (RAN). The decision in this Office action as to the patentability or unpatentability of any original patent claim, any proposed amended claim and any new claim in this proceeding is a FINAL DECISION.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment can be made in response to the RAN (37 CFR 1.953(c)). No affidavit or other evidence may be submitted after the RAN except as provided by 37 CFR 1.981 or 41.77(b)(1). Each party has thirty days or one month (whichever longer) to file a notice of appeal; cross-appeal rules (14 days after service) apply. Appeals must identify claims appealed and be signed by appropriate party/attorney. Failure to file timely notice of appeal/cross-appeal results in loss of right to appeal; if no party files timely appeal, reexamination prosecution is terminated and Director will issue and publish certificate under 37 CFR 1.997.

rubrics_metrics.name: No receipt of rebuttal brief — forwarding to Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant(s) was given a period of one month from the mailing date of the examiner’s answer within which to file a rebuttal brief; no rebuttal brief has been received within that time period. Accordingly, the reexamination proceeding is being forwarded to the Board for decision on the appeal(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.67.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods for seeking court review or rehearing have lapsed — NIRC issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: The periods for seeking court review of, or a rehearing of, the decision of the Board rendered [1] have expired and no further action has been taken by any party to the appeal. Accordingly, the appeal in this reexamination proceeding is considered terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) is issued in accordance with MPEP § 2687 to terminate the present reexamination prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of service in inter partes — requirement and timing (37 CFR 1.903)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission filed [1] is defective because it appears that the submission was not served on [2]. After the filing of a request for inter partes reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party as provided in 37 CFR 1.248. See 37 CFR 1.903.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service of the submission and a certificate of service must be provided to the Office within ONE MONTH from the date of this letter or within the time remaining in the response period of the last Office action (if applicable), whichever is longer. Insert 'patent owner' or 'third party requester' in bracket 2 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendment accompanying Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s amendment to the record appears below. The changes made by this examiner’s amendment will be reflected in the reexamination certificate to issue in due course. [1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution remains closed. Any further reply/comments by any party will not be considered and may be returned to the party that submitted it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation in inter partes
rubrics_metrics.description: The following is an examiner’s statement of reasons for patentability and/or confirmation of the claims found patentable in this reexamination proceeding: [1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph may be used as an attachment to the Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate, PTOL-2068 (item number 3). Patent owner may submit comments labeled appropriately; examiner contact instructions noted (Central Reexamination Unit telephone).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for response under 37 CFR 41.77(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods for response to this determination are identified in 37 CFR 41.77(e). Following expiration, the proceeding will be returned to the Board for reconsideration under 37 CFR 41.77(f). Note that under 41.77(e), patent owner and third party requester responsive comments are due one month from the mailing date of this determination, and replies are then due one month from date of service of the comments. These time periods cannot be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.77(g). Form paragraph 26.75.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNQ (Substantial New Question) — reasons for finding no SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: [1], as presented in the request, does not raise a substantial new question of patentability because [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert name/description for item of information (patent, application publication, non-patent literature, receipt/invoice, affidavit/declaration, transcript, or discussion regarding 35 U.S.C. 101). Insert reasons in bracket 2. Use form paragraph 28.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNQ — reasons for finding a SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: [1], as presented in the request, raises a substantial new question of patentability affecting patent claim(s) [2] because [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert item identification; bracket 2 insert claims affected; bracket 3 insert reasons why item raises SNQ. If SNQ affects only a portion of claims, explain both why SNQ found for some claims and not for others. Use form paragraph 28.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination ordered pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 257 (supplemental examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental examination proceeding, filed on [1], concluded with issuance of the supplemental examination certificate on [2]. The certificate indicated that one or more items of information submitted as part of the request for supplemental examination raises a substantial new question of patentability. Accordingly, ex parte reexamination of claim(s) [3] of U.S. Patent No. [4] is ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 257(b) and 37 CFR 1.625(b). This ex parte reexamination proceeding is initiated by the mailing of this order and will be conducted in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530 through 1.570, subject to exceptions enumerated in 37 CFR 1.625(d).
